# Minimum sample size for testing R² = 0 in linear regression
# H₀: ρ² = 0 vs H₁: ρ² ≠ 0
# Using noncentral F-test

# Parameters
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90
p <- 3  # number of predictors
R_squared <- 0.09  # anticipated R² = 0.30²
multiple_correlation <- 0.30

# Function to compute power for a given sample size
compute_power <- function(N, alpha, p, R_squared) {
  # Degrees of freedom
  df1 <- p  # numerator (number of predictors)
  df2 <- N - p - 1  # denominator (N - number of parameters including intercept)
  
  # Critical value from F-distribution under null hypothesis
  F_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  # λ = R² * (N - p - 1) / (1 - R²)
  lambda <- R_squared * (N - p - 1) / (1 - R_squared)
  
  # Power = P(F > F_crit | λ) under noncentral F-distribution
  power <- 1 - pf(F_crit, df1, df2, lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum sample size
# Start with a reasonable guess and refine
N_min <- 50
N_max <- 500

# Binary search or linear search for efficiency
results <- data.frame(N = integer(), power = numeric())

for (N in N_min:N_max) {
  power <- compute_power(N, alpha, p, R_squared)
  results <- rbind(results, data.frame(N = N, power = power))
  
  # Stop once we've clearly found the minimum
  if (N > 100 && power >= target_power) {
    break
  }
}

# Find the minimum N meeting target power
minimum_N <- results$N[results$power >= target_power][1]
achieved_power <- results$power[results$N == minimum_N]

# Also compute power at N-1 to verify this is the minimum admissible
power_at_N_minus_1 <- compute_power(minimum_N - 1, alpha, p, R_squared)

cat("Sample Size Search Results:\n")
cat("============================\n")
cat(sprintf("Minimum sample size for 90%% power: %d\n", minimum_N))
cat(sprintf("Achieved power at N = %d: %.4f\n", minimum_N, achieved_power))
cat(sprintf("Power at N = %d: %.4f\n", minimum_N - 1, power_at_N_minus_1))
cat("\nSelected design details:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Total sample size: %d participants\n", minimum_N))
cat(sprintf("  Number of predictors: %d\n", p))
cat(sprintf("  Anticipated R²: %.4f (ρ = %.2f)\n", R_squared, multiple_correlation))
cat(sprintf("  Significance level α: %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("  Target power: %.2f\n", target_power))
cat(sprintf("  Numerator df: %d\n", p))
cat(sprintf("  Denominator df: %d\n", minimum_N - p - 1))
cat(sprintf("  Noncentrality parameter λ: %.4f\n", 
            R_squared * (minimum_N - p - 1) / (1 - R_squared)))

# Output for structured result
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = minimum_N, unit = "participants_total"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(achieved_power, 4), unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "power_at_N_minus_1", value = round(power_at_N_minus_1, 4), unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "number_of_predictors", value = p, unit = "count"),
    list(metric = "population_R_squared", value = R_squared, unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "significance_level", value = alpha, unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "target_power", value = target_power, unit = "probability")
  )),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

p <- 3  # number of predictors

# Function to compute power using noncentral F-distribution
# Test statistic: F = [R² / p] / [(1 - R²) / (N - p - 1)]
#               = R² × (N - p - 1) / [p × (1 - R²)]
# Under H₁ with true R², this follows F(p, N - p - 1, λ)
# where λ = R² × (N - p - 1) / (1 - R²)

power_noncentralF <- function(N, alpha, p, R_sq) {
  df_num <- p
  df_den <- N - p - 1
  
  # Critical F-value under null hypothesis (λ = 0)
  F_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df_num, df_den)
  
  # Noncentrality parameter under alternative
  lambda <- R_sq * df_den / (1 - R_sq)
  
  # Power: Pr(F > F_crit | λ)
  power <- 1 - pf(F_crit, df_num, df_den, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(list(power = power, F_crit = F_crit, lambda = lambda))
}

# Minimum sample size for testing R² = 0 in linear regression
# H₀: ρ² = 0 vs H₁: ρ² ≠ 0
# Using noncentral F-test

# Parameters
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90
p <- 3  # number of predictors
R_squared <- 0.09  # anticipated R² = 0.30²
multiple_correlation <- 0.30

# Function to compute power for a given sample size
compute_power <- function(N, alpha, p, R_squared) {
  # Degrees of freedom
  df1 <- p  # numerator (number of predictors)
  df2 <- N - p - 1  # denominator (N - number of parameters including intercept)
  
  # Critical value from F-distribution under null hypothesis
  F_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  # λ = R² * (N - p - 1) / (1 - R²)
  lambda <- R_squared * (N - p - 1) / (1 - R_squared)
  
  # Power = P(F > F_crit | λ) under noncentral F-distribution
  power <- 1 - pf(F_crit, df1, df2, lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum sample size
# Start with a reasonable guess and refine

N_max <- 500

for (N in N_min:N_max) {

# Evidence e1; success=true

# Minimum sample size for testing R² = 0 in linear regression
# H₀: ρ² = 0 vs H₁: ρ² ≠ 0
# Using noncentral F-test

# Parameters
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90
p <- 3  # number of predictors
R_squared <- 0.09  # anticipated R² = 0.30²
multiple_correlation <- 0.30

# Function to compute power for a given sample size
compute_power <- function(N, alpha, p, R_squared) {
  # Degrees of freedom
  df1 <- p  # numerator (number of predictors)
  df2 <- N - p - 1  # denominator (N - number of parameters including intercept)
  
  # Critical value from F-distribution under null hypothesis
  F_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  # λ = R² * (N - p - 1) / (1 - R²)
  lambda <- R_squared * (N - p - 1) / (1 - R_squared)
  
  # Power = P(F > F_crit | λ) under noncentral F-distribution
  power <- 1 - pf(F_crit, df1, df2, lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum sample size
# Start with a reasonable guess and refine
N_min <- 50
N_max <- 500

# Binary search or linear search for efficiency
results <- data.frame(N = integer(), power = numeric())

for (N in N_min:N_max) {
  power <- compute_power(N, alpha, p, R_squared)
  results <- rbind(results, data.frame(N = N, power = power))
  
  # Stop once we've clearly found the minimum
  if (N > 100 && power >= target_power) {
    break
  }
}

# Find the minimum N meeting target power
minimum_N <- results$N[results$power >= target_power][1]
achieved_power <- results$power[results$N == minimum_N]

# Also compute power at N-1 to verify this is the minimum admissible
power_at_N_minus_1 <- compute_power(minimum_N - 1, alpha, p, R_squared)

cat("Sample Size Search Results:\n")
cat("============================\n")
cat(sprintf("Minimum sample size for 90%% power: %d\n", minimum_N))
cat(sprintf("Achieved power at N = %d: %.4f\n", minimum_N, achieved_power))
cat(sprintf("Power at N = %d: %.4f\n", minimum_N - 1, power_at_N_minus_1))
cat("\nSelected design details:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Total sample size: %d participants\n", minimum_N))
cat(sprintf("  Number of predictors: %d\n", p))
cat(sprintf("  Anticipated R²: %.4f (ρ = %.2f)\n", R_squared, multiple_correlation))
cat(sprintf("  Significance level α: %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("  Target power: %.2f\n", target_power))
cat(sprintf("  Numerator df: %d\n", p))
cat(sprintf("  Denominator df: %d\n", minimum_N - p - 1))
cat(sprintf("  Noncentrality parameter λ: %.4f\n", 
            R_squared * (minimum_N - p - 1) / (1 - R_squared)))

# Output for structured result
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = minimum_N, unit = "participants_total"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(achieved_power, 4), unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "power_at_N_minus_1", value = round(power_at_N_minus_1, 4), unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "number_of_predictors", value = p, unit = "count"),
    list(metric = "population_R_squared", value = R_squared, unit = "proportion"),

    list(metric = "target_power", value = target_power, unit = "probability")
  )),
